QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_32

question.text: Net IRR is below Gross IRR by a LARGER percentage (~50%) in the Worst-case scenario than the Best-case scenario. Why?

answer.text: Fixed expenses eat a bigger share of smaller gross returns
Tax rates are higher in worst case

explanation.text: The Logic: Fixed costs (set-up, yearly expenses, management fees) don't scale down with performance — in a lower-return year they consume a larger share of returns. The Trap: Fees don't drop proportionally; tax rates are identical. Cross-Exam Context: Key behavioural finance insight (XV/X-A). Distributor's Pro-Tip: Show the worst-case scenario in distribution presentations so clients grasp fee drag in down markets.
